quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: How can you help reduce road rage?

options.text: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes.
Talk on your cell phone while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes.
questions.explanation: To help prevent road rage, follow traffic laws, signs, and signals. Always use your turn signal when changing lanes.

questions.question: What is the only proven way to remove alcohol or drugs from your system?
questions.explanation: Alcohol leaves your body slowly. Cold showers, coffee, and exercise do not lower blood alcohol content. The only way to reduce alcohol in your system is to wait.

questions.question: Before changing lanes or passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Check your blind spots and mirrors.
Signal your intention before changing lanes.

questions.explanation: Before any lane change, use your turn signal. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: A driving distraction is:

options.text: Anything that makes you swerve while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving. Distractions can cause crashes, injuries, and death.

questions.question: Construction and maintenance work zone signs are:
questions.explanation: All temporary work zone signs have orange backgrounds with black writing and symbols.

questions.question: In rain or fog, drivers should use:
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain, snow, or fog. High beams reflect off precipitation and reduce visibility.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines down the center of a road mean passing is:
questions.explanation: A double yellow centerline means no vehicle can cross it to pass.

questions.question: When double solid yellow lines separate lanes of traffic:

options.text: Passing is allowed from the left.
Passing is allowed from the right.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid lines mean traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.question: Why should drivers give extra space to children on bicycles?

options.text: Children do not have the same reflexes as adults.
Children are smaller and harder to see.

questions.explanation: Children are unpredictable and hard to see. Watch for them near schools, bus stops, parks, and playgrounds. Children on bikes may suddenly enter the road.

questions.question: A red traffic light means drivers should:

options.text: Speed up to clear the intersection.

questions.explanation: Stop at a red light and wait until it changes to green.

questions.question: A pedestrian is crossing after the "Don't Walk" signal starts to flash. They are in the middle of the street when your light turns green. You should:

options.text: Go because you have the right-of-way.
Go if the pedestrian is not in your lane.
Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing.
questions.explanation: At a green light, yield to anyone already in the intersection. Wait until pedestrians have crossed before moving forward.

questions.question: You must yield to a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog:

options.text: Only when the guide dog is leading them.
Only if a crossing guard is present.

questions.explanation: Pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes must always be given the right-of-way.

questions.question: You must stop your vehicle:

options.text: When a police officer signals you to stop.

questions.explanation: Stop at red lights and always obey police officers directing traffic.

questions.question: When driving on gravel or dirt roads:

options.text: Your tires grip better than on pavement.
Your tires have less grip, so you must slow down.
Visibility is better than on pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires have less grip, so you must slow down.
questions.explanation: Tires have less grip on gravel and dirt. Slow down because stopping takes longer and turning is easier to skid.

questions.question: Which substances can affect your ability to drive?

options.text: Cough syrup and cold tablets with codeine or antihistamines.

questions.explanation: Many drugs impair driving. These include prescription medications like tranquilizers and sedatives, over-the-counter cold and allergy medicines, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: You must obey school crossing guards:

options.text: Unless you do not see children.

questions.explanation: Always obey crossing guards near schools.

questions.question: When you have a green light and pedestrians are in the intersection:
questions.explanation: With a green light, yield to anyone already in the intersection. Yield to pedestrians when turning on a steady green signal.

questions.question: When merging onto an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
Merge across two lanes at once.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
questions.explanation: Find a large enough gap to safely enter traffic. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless there are no safe gaps.

questions.question: If you are angry after an argument, you should:

options.text: Play loud music so you won't think about it.
Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.
Drive on the interstate to let off steam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.
questions.explanation: Your emotions affect your driving ability. If you are angry, upset, or worried, calm down before driving so you can focus.

questions.question: If you encounter an aggressive driver, you should:
questions.explanation: When you encounter an aggressive driver, the safest choice is to get out of their way. Never compete with other drivers.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in work zones?

options.text: Speed up to get through quickly.
Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
Keep driving at your normal speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you enter a work zone. Follow the posted speed limits and watch for hazards. Workers may be present.

questions.question: You must remove snow, frost, and ice from:

options.text: Just the windshield and passenger window.

questions.explanation: You must see clearly from all windows before driving. Clean snow, ice, and frost from all windows and mirrors.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and drugs?
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows the nervous system. It reduces alertness, increases reaction time, and reduces coordination.

questions.question: This sign warns of one type of:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to conditions ahead. This sign warns that another road crosses the highway ahead.

questions.question: When passing a large truck, you should:

options.text: Return to your lane and slow down right away.
Give the truck plenty of space before returning to your lane.
Return to your lane whenever you want.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the truck plenty of space before returning to your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not return to your lane too quickly. See the entire front of the truck in your mirror before changing lanes. Trucks need twice as much space to stop as other vehicles.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign is displayed on slow-moving vehicles.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the road means:
questions.explanation: Solid yellow lines mark zones where passing is not allowed. If the solid line is on your side, you cannot pass.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Wet roads are slippery and dangerous. Slow down on wet pavement because it takes longer to stop.

questions.question: A red curb means:

options.text: The area is for picking up or dropping off passengers.

questions.explanation: You cannot stop, stand, or park at a red curb.

questions.question: What do rumble strips do?

options.text: They alert drivers to tire problems.
They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.
They alert inattentive drivers with vibration and sound that their vehicle has left the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They alert inattentive drivers with vibration and sound that their vehicle has left the road.
questions.explanation: Rumble strips make noise and vibrations to warn drowsy or inattentive drivers that they are leaving the road or approaching a stop sign or signal.

questions.question: Which statement is correct?

options.text: Use your left foot to brake.
Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
questions.explanation: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating. Apply brakes gently with increasing pressure for a smooth stop.

questions.question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, you should:

options.text: Use your horn to get attention from other cars.
Get out and flag down the first passing vehicle.
Pull off the road, turn on emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road, turn on emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Turn on emergency flashers to warn other drivers and stay inside your vehicle. Walking on an interstate is very dangerous because of high-speed traffic.

questions.question: If the road ahead is flooded, you should:

options.text: Do not drive through. Turn around and find another route.
Drive only in the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive through. Turn around and find another route.
questions.explanation: Never drive on a flooded road. Water may hide hazards. Find another route.

questions.question: This sign is a:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to conditions ahead that may require you to change your driving.

questions.question: This bicyclist is signaling:
questions.explanation: Bicyclists use hand and arm signals. A straight left arm means a left turn.

questions.question: Before stopping at a traffic signal or sign, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors for traffic around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors for traffic around you.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors first. Be aware of other drivers as you slow down. Then press the brake for a smooth stop.

questions.question: Like alcohol and drugs, drowsiness can:
questions.explanation: Not getting enough sleep causes poor driving. Sleepiness slows reaction time, reduces awareness, and impairs judgment.

questions.question: What is a crosswalk?

options.text: Another name for a four-way intersection.
An area for road construction workers.
The area where pedestrians may cross the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The area where pedestrians may cross the road.
questions.explanation: Crosswalks are marked with white lines. They may be marked or unmarked.

questions.question: Should you always drive more slowly than other traffic?

options.text: No, driving too slowly can block traffic.
Yes, it is a good defensive technique.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, driving too slowly can block traffic.
questions.explanation: Slow down in heavy traffic or bad weather. But do not drive so slowly that you block the normal flow of traffic, or you may get a ticket.

questions.question: Before taking medicine and driving, you should:

options.text: Ask your doctor about how it affects driving.
Keep your window open and drive slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask your doctor about how it affects driving.
questions.explanation: Both prescription and over-the-counter medicines can impair driving. Always ask your doctor or pharmacist how a medicine will affect your ability to drive.
